messages.content: What is the freezing point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure, provided in kilopascals (kPa) or atmospheres (atm). Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The chemical name of the substance for which to calculate the boiling point, such as 'water' or 'ethanol'.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water is essentially unchanged from its standard‑pressure value.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid equilibrium:

\[
\frac{dP}{dT}=\frac{\Delta H_f}{T\,\Delta V}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\;
\frac{dT}{dP}\approx-0.07\;\text{K / MPa}
\]

A pressure change of 0.01 MPa (10 kPa) therefore lowers the melting temperature by only

\[
\Delta T \approx -0.07\;\text{K / MPa}\times0.01\;\text{MPa}\approx -7\times10^{-4}\;\text{K}
\]

So the freezing point is about **–0.0007 °C**, i.e. essentially **0 °C** for all practical purposes.
